requirement:
Habeas MUST locate its per-user configuration at
`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/habeas/config.toml` on Unix when XDG_CONFIG_HOME is an absolute,
nonempty path, otherwise at `$HOME/.config/habeas/config.toml`. On Windows it MUST
use `%APPDATA%/habeas/config.toml`. `HOME` and `APPDATA` MUST likewise be
absolute, nonempty paths to be used. If no usable base directory can be
determined, an operation requiring user configuration MUST fail with an
explanatory diagnostic naming the variable.

The same user configuration MUST be usable across projects. Its location MUST
NOT be selected relative to the current project or changed by project settings.
User-local preferences for a project MAY remain in the user configuration;
workspace settings MUST use `habeas.toml` under
{cite}`requirements.configuration.workspace_location`.
rationale:
I judge the tests adequate for `requirements.configuration.user_location`. I did not read any implementation source, and I did not run the tests. Every obligation maps to a marked test with assertions on the outcome.

**Unix location**
- `tests/configuration.rs#fn[locations_use_absolute_xdg_values_and_platform_fallbacks]` asserts that an absolute `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` gives `config/habeas/config.toml`.
- The same test loops over `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` set to `""` and `"relative"`. Each time it asserts the fallback `home/.config/habeas/config.toml`.
- It also asserts the fallback when only `HOME` is set.
- `fn[base_directories_must_be_absolute_and_nonempty]` repeats the relative-XDG fallback to an absolute `HOME`.

**Windows location**
- `fn[locations_use_absolute_xdg_values_and_platform_fallbacks]` asserts that `APPDATA` gives `<APPDATA>/habeas/config.toml` on `ConfigPlatform::Windows`.

**`HOME` and `APPDATA` must be absolute and nonempty**
- `fn[base_directories_must_be_absolute_and_nonempty]` tries `""` and `"relative/home"` for `HOME` on Unix and for `APPDATA` on Windows.
- It asserts an error each time, and the error text must contain the variable name.

**Failure with a diagnostic naming the variable**
- `fn[locations_use_absolute_xdg_values_and_platform_fallbacks]` calls `user_config_path_from` with no variables set. It asserts the error names `HOME` on Unix and `APPDATA` on Windows.
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[authoring_uses_the_same_user_config_path_in_different_projects]` covers this end to end. It removes `HOME`, `APPDATA` and `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, runs `author`, and asserts an unrecorded failure whose output names `HOME` (or `APPDATA` on Windows).

**Same configuration across projects, not project-relative or changed by project settings**
- The same end-to-end test creates two separate project fixtures. The second has its own `habeas.toml`.
- Both are pointed at the first fixture's config directory, which holds an invalid config.
- Both runs must fail naming that same config path. A location chosen relative to the project, or moved by project settings, would not produce that result.

**Clauses with no test of their own**
- The workspace clause (`workspace_location`) is cited context, so I did not reassess it.
- The `MAY` clause allowing user-local project preferences imposes nothing to test.

I found no unacknowledged gap.

`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/habeas/config.toml` on Unix when XDG_CONFIG_HOME is an absolute,
nonempty path, otherwise at `$HOME/.config/habeas/config.toml`. On Windows it MUST
use `%APPDATA%/habeas/config.toml`. `HOME` and `APPDATA` MUST likewise be
absolute, nonempty paths to be used. If no usable base directory can be
determined, an operation requiring user configuration MUST fail with an
explanatory diagnostic naming the variable.
The same user configuration MUST be usable across projects. Its location MUST
NOT be selected relative to the current project or changed by project settings.
User-local preferences for a project MAY remain in the user configuration;
workspace settings MUST use `habeas.toml` under
{cite}`requirements.configuration.workspace_location`.
:::{req} workspace_location
Habeas MUST search from its invocation directory upward for the nearest enclosing
`habeas.toml`. It MUST use that file alone, without merging ancestor workspace
files. A library operation given a project root MUST search from that root unless
its current directory is inside the project, in which case it MUST start there.
The directory containing the selected file defines the base for its relative
paths; it does not replace the Cargo and mdBook project root. A missing file MUST
mean absent workspace settings. Discovery MUST report unreadable candidate files
rather than silently selecting an ancestor. Loading MUST NOT create the file.
